name: FedEx Express World Hub - Memphis TN

fieldNotes.siteConfirmation: Roster point lands on the main sort building of the FedEx Express World Hub on the west side of Memphis International Airport. Confirmed via satellite (multiple sort buildings, 100+ parked freighter aircraft positions, ULD/container staging acres) and web research (FedEx newsroom: largest sort facility in the global network, ~940 acres, 171 aircraft gates, 13,000 team members, 84 miles of conveyor).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Hardened secured campus. FedEx Main Screening Facility (Flintco-built, 44,000 SF) is the main controlled point of entry. Street View shows steel anti-ram palisade fencing with outriggers, chain-link with coiled razor wire, Jersey-barrier lane channelization on internal roads, and a canopied vehicle checkpoint with multiple lanes.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Dedicated 44,000 SF Main Screening Facility staffed checkpoint = staffed guard facility (well beyond a simple booth). Multiple manned checkpoints exist for the 5-mile perimeter.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Vehicle screening checkpoint at perimeter, then secondary controlled access into airside operations areas — multi-stage controlled access.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: This is an air-to-ground hub; primary cargo transfer is aircraft-side. Landside truck docks for road feeder vehicles exist but are dispersed across sort buildings; door count is an estimate from imagery (50+ band).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive road feeder vehicle / trailer staging visible between sort buildings and in landside lots; well into 50+ band. Counts approximate.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of 8+ large buildings: original superhub sort building, new 1.3M sq ft automated sort facility (2024), maintenance hangars, screening facility, support/office buildings.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 940 acres per FedEx newsroom; perimeter box is an approximation of the core landside operations footprint and the published campus figure was used.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the property; airside facility.
